This is the photo that haunts me most…. the last taken before the second tower collapsed.

Dad was FDNY Rescue 3. Rescue companies are the FDNY’s elite, each firefighter was had three additional specialties. Two shared by everyone in the truck - HAZMAT & Collapse for R3 - and one from civilian life (Dad’s was Major Trauma).

After getting promoted he helped create a dedicated HAZMAT unit as covering LT. 

Then a roof collapse crushed Dad’s spine and he was moved to a desk job at Emergency Services. He hated riding a desk but poured his passion into getting a dedicated purpose built Collapse Unit truck for R3: a rolling lumberyard of shoring, jacks, saws and rescue gear.

Often he worked from home and I would return from high school with sketches and spreadsheets of a collapse truck spread out across the dining room table. We would talk about it until mom told us to clear the table for dinner. 

In 1995 his plans materialized and Rescue 3 got the truck but his cancer became terminal and I was away at college so we missed the commissioning. 

This was before the internet so I only saw a photo of the truck twice. His FDNY brother Eddie Sere, showed me one at his funeral and I saw it again when I turned on my TV the morning of 9/11

This truck. 

On 9/11, it was FDNY’s only dedicated Collapse Unit but was buried in the rubble of the north tower before it could be used. 

Every man of Rescue 3 manning the truck that day perished in the collapse.
